subject: Follow-up: post-demo model-fit notes + performance pack & next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finlytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + quick deliverables

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary goal: automate extraction of transaction metadata and classification for regulatory reporting (50k docs/day peak).
- Success metrics: >95% entity-extraction F1 on your audit set, <250ms p95 inference latency for a 1k token window, predictable cost under $0.XX/token (we'll tune).

Deliverables I can share by EOD Monday:
1) Redwood-verified performance pack (latency percentiles, TPS at common sequence lengths) tailored to your throughput profile.
2) Prompt set + eval harness we used in today’s demo (small sample) — so you can run locally.
3) Initial mutual action plan (timeline + procurement milestones).

Short list of models I recommend based on today's discussion (initial heuristics):
- redwood-2.7b-q4: best cost/throughput tradeoff for extractive tasks — approx 150–180 TPS (seq=512, batch=8), p95 ~210ms.
- mistral-7b-8k: stronger instruction-following on long context; ~75–95 TPS, p95 ~350ms.
- llm-13b-high-qual: better accuracy on edge cases but higher latency — ~30–45 TPS, p95 ~520ms.

Notes on quality/regression risk:
- Prompt sensitivity on payment-description extraction: we saw a 3–4% delta in F1 between prompt variants A/B in our small eval.
- Hallucination risk lower for extractive templates but increases with free-form summarization.

Links and attachments: I’ve dropped the perf CSV and a prompt-set sample in the attachments and uploaded the full pack to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B-finlytics-eval-pack

Next immediate asks from you:
- Confirm a snapshot of your sample audit set that we can use for a short, scoped PoC (PII redacted).
- Procurement contact and initial purchase window (Q3 vs Q4).

I’ll loop Marissa for the deeper perf notes and Priyom for procurement coordination.

Best,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Head of Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finlytics.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 17:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick deliverables

Vivek — really helpful, thanks. A few quick clarifications: 

1) Our peak 50k docs/day often spikes during end-of-month closes; latency target is "interactive" for the dashboard (sub-300ms p95) but for batch jobs we can accept higher p95 if throughput scales.
2) We can share a redacted sample by Monday COB; procurement is interested in an FAQ sheet on data residency and SOC evidence before we talk dollars.

We prefer starting with a small PoC (2 weeks) that validates entity extraction and cost-per-doc. Can you include an explicit PoC success criteria section in the MAP? Also please add estimated token cost per 1M tokens for each recommended model variant.

Thanks — Alyssa
Alyssa Turner
Product Lead, Data Ops | Finlytics

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick deliverables

Thanks Alyssa — attaching the first-pass artifacts and answers inline below. Forwarding perf snippets to Marissa for the model-level breakdown.

--- Forwarded attachment list ---
Attachments: redwood-verified-profiles.csv (CSV summary), finlytics-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (sample prompts), cost-estimate-first-pass.xlsx

Quick answers: 
- PoC success criteria (proposed):
  * Entity extraction F1 >= 95% on your redacted audit set (evaluated on a held-out 2k sample).
  * Dashboard latency: p95 <= 300ms for interactive routes (seq ~512, batch <=4).
  * Processing cost <= $X per 1k docs (we’ll refine with tokens-per-doc after we get the sample).

- Token-cost estimates (very approximate; includes average tokenization for your docs):
  * redwood-2.7b-q4: ~$12 per 1M tokens (in our hosted pricing model), high throughput.
  * mistral-7b-8k: ~$28 per 1M tokens, better long-context accuracy.
  * llm-13b-high-qual: ~$72 per 1M tokens, higher accuracy for edge-case language patterns.

Performance pack highlights (extracted rows from redwood-verified-profiles.csv):
- redwood-2.7b-q4 (seq=512, batch=8): median latency 40ms, p95 210ms, p99 380ms, throughput 150–180 TPS (tokens/sec equivalent measured on A100-like instance).
- mistral-7b-8k (seq=2048, batch=4): median 120ms, p95 350ms, p99 620ms, throughput 75–95 TPS.
- llm-13b-high-qual (seq=512, batch=2): median 160ms, p95 520ms, p99 900ms, throughput 30–45 TPS.

Quality notes for Marissa: we observed the largest gap vs. baseline on payment-reference disambiguation (prompt A failed ~4% more often than prompt B). We recommend adding a small rule-based pass to normalize vendor names in the PoC to reduce annotation noise.

Links: full per-model CSV + profile viewer: https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profiles/finlytics-FD-2027-129

Next steps I propose:
1) Finlytics shares redacted sample by Mon COB (you indicated yes).
2) Redwood provisions a scoped PoC workspace (we'll seed with the prompt set and perf configs) by Wed.
3) Two-week PoC runs -> short results review -> procurement/contract conversation.

Marissa — can you validate the perf rows and suggest preferred quantization/latency knobs for the PoC? Priyom — can you share a short procurement checklist and expected procurement lead time for a mid-market deal (ballpark)?

-Vivek

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@finlytics.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + quick deliverables

On Sat, Jun 19, 2027 at 09:30 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Performance pack highlights (extracted rows from redwood-verified-profiles.csv):
> - redwood-2.7b-q4 (seq=512, batch=8): median latency 40ms, p95 210ms, p99 380ms, throughput 150–180 TPS
> - mistral-7b-8k (seq=2048, batch=4): median 120ms, p95 350ms, p99 620ms, throughput 75–95 TPS
> - llm-13b-high-qual (seq=512, batch=2): median 160ms, p95 520ms, p99 900ms, throughput 30–45 TPS

Adding a few clarifications for the PoC config and knobs: 
- For the PoC start, default to redwood-2.7b-q4 with prefix/KV cache enabled and batch cap of 8. That will give you highest token-efficiency and lowest median latency.
- If you need stronger few-shot instruction behavior for reconciliation tasks, fall back to mistral-7b-8k for the reconciliation path only (we can route those calls).
- We'll enable token-amount-based throttles to keep p95 under 300ms for interactive endpoints.

Regression monitoring: I added a minimal eval set to the Drive folder and a quick-run Quality dashboard link (in the Drive). Please review the prompt variants labeled A/B/C — A matched the demo, B includes vendor-normalization, C is stricter (higher precision).

I’ll prepare a short README in the Drive explaining how to rerun the perf harness and where the p95/p99 numbers come from (measurement windows, instance type).

-Marissa
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

Short checklist:

- SOC2 Type II evidence + data processing addendum (we can provide current reports; expect a standard DPA).

Ballpark lead times: legal review + PO issuance ~7–14 days after PoC acceptance. If procurement needs vendor setup forms, send them to procurement@finlytics.com and I’ll work the intake.

I'll draft the MAP with the procurement milestones and share early next week.

Thanks — Priyom
